definitions.gloss: to greet; to say a few words of greeting (at an event)
definitions.explanation: To greet someone when meeting or parting, or to pay one's respects with a short formal speech or visit (at a ceremony, on starting a job, on moving in).

examples.english: In the morning I greeted the people I met.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{新郎|しんろう}→新郎：12982_shinrou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{挨拶|あいさつ}した。
examples.english: At the wedding, the groom's father gave a short speech.

examples.japanese: ⟦{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}したら→引っ越す：01171_hikkosu⟧、⟦{近所|きんじょ}→近所：01318_kinjo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{挨拶|あいさつ}し⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}きましょう→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: When you move in, go around and say hello to the neighbors.

examples.japanese: ⟦{隣|となり}→隣：01003_tonari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{挨拶|あいさつ}した⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{返事|へんじ}→返事：00844_henji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦なかった→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: I greeted my neighbor, but there was no reply.

notes:
{挨拶|あいさつ}する covers more than saying hello: it is also paying one's respects, including the short formal speech given at a ceremony or event.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Intransitive; the person greeted takes ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{挨拶|あいさつ}する
- Exchanging greetings: ⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{交|か}わす→交わす：19373_kawasu⟧

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦おはようございます→おはようございます：30844_ohayougozaimasu⟧: Good morning
- ⟦こんにちは→こんにちは：02839_konnichiha⟧: Hello (daytime)
- ⟦こんばんは→こんばんは：27858_konbanha⟧: Good evening
- ⟦さようなら→さようなら：10531_sayounara⟧: Goodbye

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to greet (the same meaning, with ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧)
- ⟦{開会|かいかい}→開会：04118_kaikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧: opening address
- ⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go and pay one's respects (to new neighbors, clients, a teacher)

CULTURAL NOTE: Greetings matter a great deal in Japanese schools and workplaces and are usually accompanied by a bow. Moving into a new home or starting a new job is marked by visiting people to {挨拶|あいさつ}する, often with a small gift.
